title: Microsoft Teams: private chat for organisers and presenters in webinars, structured meetings and town halls
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap, Microsoft's tenant notice and the documentation checked. It correctly distinguishes private event group chat from attendee chat, preserves the meeting-options update condition, and identifies the Teams Rooms Pro requirement on Android. The undocumented backroom control and the conflicting attendee-chat defaults are reported rather than guessed.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Manage chat for Teams events excludes event group chat from its attendee-chat storage rule.
claims.quote: Meeting chat messages in events optimized for large audiences, excluding the event group chat, are stored only in an organizer's mailbox for up to 30 days.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Microsoft's general Teams group-chat documentation places compliance copies in chat participants' Exchange Online mailboxes.
claims.quote: Exchange Online stores Teams compliance records that the substrate captures, and eDiscovery can access these records. ... Messages in group chats are stored in the Exchange Online mailbox of all chat participants.

claims.claim: External presenter support for event group chat is covered by a separate roadmap item.
claims.quote: 573706: Microsoft Teams: External presenter support for event group chat. Event group chat, the private chat for organizers, co-organizers, and presenters in an event or structured meeting, will support external presenters.

claims.claim: The change is person-to-person chat rather than an autonomous action capability.
claims.quote: Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters can chat privately in a separate chat from attendees. This chat is available to access before, during, and after the event.
